title: Sakuranin Is a Novel Anti-Inflammatory Agent Targeting TLR4-NF-kappaB Signaling Pathways.
authors: Jayasingha, Jayasingha Arachchige Chathuranga Chanaka; Lee, Kyoung Tae; Jin, Cheng-Yun; Choi, Yung Hyun; Lee, Chang Soo; Kim, Gi-Young
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Sakuranin通过靶向TLR4-NF-kappaB信号通路的抗炎机制，涉及分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Sakuranin (SKR) is naturally occurring compound known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities; however, its precise molecular mechanisms in modulating inflammation through toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) signaling remain unclear. This study investigates the anti-inflammatory effects of SKR in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages and zebrafish larvae, focusing on the TLR4-nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kappaB) signaling pathway. SKR significantly inhibited the production of nitric oxide (NO), prostaglandin E(2) (PGE(2)), interleukin-12 (IL-12), and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-alpha), while downregulating the expression of inducible NO synthase (NOS2) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX2) at both transcriptional and translational levels. In vivo, SKR reduced LPS-induced mortality, restored cardiac function, and attenuated immune cell infiltration in zebrafish larvae, further underscoring its systemic anti-inflammatory effects. Mechanistic studies revealed that SKR inhibited NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and directly interacted with the TLR4/myeloid differentiation factor 2 (MD2) complex, thereby disrupting LPS-TLR4 signaling. Molecular docking and colocalization analyses confirmed that SKR directly binds TLR4, potentially interfering with LPS recognition and downstream pro-inflammatory signaling activation. Collectively, these findings highlight SKR as a potent modulator of TLR4-mediated inflammation, offering promising therapeutic potential for inflammatory disorders. Further investigations into its pharmacokinetics, bioavailability, and long-term efficacy in chronic inflammatory conditions are warranted to support its clinical applications.
abstract_zh: Sakuranin (SKR) 是一种天然化合物，以其抗炎和抗氧化活性而闻名；然而，其通过toll样受体4 (TLR4) 信号通路调节炎症的精确分子机制仍不清楚。本研究探讨了SKR在脂多糖 (LPS) 刺激的RAW 264.7巨噬细胞和斑马鱼幼鱼中的抗炎作用，重点关注TLR4-核因子-kappa B (NF-kappaB) 信号通路。SKR显著抑制了一氧化氮 (NO)、前列腺素E(2) (PGE(2))、白细胞介素-12 (IL-12) 和肿瘤坏死因子-alpha (TNF-alpha) 的产生，同时在转录和翻译水平上下调诱导型NO合酶 (NOS2) 和环氧合酶-2 (COX2) 的表达。在体内，SKR降低了LPS诱导的死亡率，恢复了心脏功能，并减弱了斑马鱼幼鱼中的免疫细胞浸润，进一步强调了其系统性抗炎作用。机制研究表明，SKR抑制了NF-kappaB的核转位，并直接与TLR4/髓样分化因子2 (MD2) 复合物相互作用，从而干扰LPS-TLR4信号传导。分子对接和共定位分析证实，SKR直接结合TLR4，可能干扰LPS识别和下游促炎信号激活。总体而言，这些发现突出了SKR作为TLR4介导炎症的有效调节剂，为炎症性疾病提供了有前景的治疗潜力。进一步研究其药代动力学、生物利用度以及在慢性炎症条件下的长期疗效，对于支持其临床应用是必要的。
